transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I, uh... I came in because I just can’t shut my brain off anymore. It's getting really exhausting. 

It usually starts with just one normal concern—like, say a client isn't responding to an email. But within minutes, my mind just spirals. I get completely convinced that I’m going to lose the contract, which means I'll fall behind on my divorce payments, and... and then I start thinking I'll never get back to a real leadership role at work. It just takes off like that, and I can't seem to stop it.

When you have these thoughts, do you ever experience sudden, overwhelming surges of physical panic—like a racing heart, chest pain, or a feeling that you are about to die—that reach a peak within minutes?

No, I don't think I've ever had that. I mean, my heart might beat a bit faster when I'm really worked up about a project or something, but... I don't get chest pain or feel like I'm going to die. It's not really a sudden surge that peaks like you're describing. It's more just a constant, draining worry that never really stops.
Over what period of time have you been experiencing this persistent, draining worry most days?

It's been about... thirteen months now. It started right when I was fired from my last job. I figured it would get better once I found this new contract work, but it never really let up. It's just been there most days since then.
Besides the constant worrying, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless, or becoming easily fatigued?

Yeah, definitely. I feel wound up almost all day. It's... it's like my shoulders are just locked tight, like I'm constantly bracing for bad news. And I definitely get restless, too. I'll catch myself pacing around the house, or I'll just sit there bouncing my leg during conference calls, even when nothing stressful is actually happening. It's just this constant physical tension.
